# Scribe

> A tiny, free, open source Mac app that transcribes your calls without a bot joining the meeting, and hands the transcript to Claude or ChatGPT with one click.

- Site: https://scribe.finereli.com
- Download (latest release v1.2.1, Oct 12 2026, signed and notarized by Apple): https://github.com/finereli/scribe/releases/latest/download/Scribe.dmg
- Source (MIT): https://github.com/finereli/scribe
- Releases and changelog: https://github.com/finereli/scribe/releases
- Author: Eli Finer, independent developer (https://finereli.com)

## What it does

Scribe records two things on your Mac: your microphone (labelled "Me") and your Mac's audio output (labelled "Them"). It transcribes both live with the speech recognizer built into macOS and shows who said what. When the call ends, a button copies the transcript with a line of context and opens Claude or ChatGPT, so you can paste it and ask your own questions.

Nothing joins the meeting, so it works on any call regardless of who hosts it or whether bots are allowed: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp desktop, FaceTime, Slack, in the app or in a browser.

## Facts

- Price: free. No trial, no paid plan, no account.
- License: MIT, open source.
- Platform: macOS 14.2 (Sonoma) or later, Apple Silicon and Intel. 14.2 added the system audio recording Scribe uses.
- Size: about 2 MB installed, about 1 MB download. No dependencies and no model to download.
- Languages: English, Hebrew, Russian (one per call). More can be added on request.
- Privacy: audio and transcripts are saved as files in a folder per call on your Mac. Scribe has no server. English is transcribed on-device. Hebrew and Russian go to Apple's speech service (the one dictation uses) unless the Mac supports on-device recognition for that language; Scribe uses on-device whenever macOS offers it.
- Speakers: Me versus Them only. Several people on the other side are all "Them".
- Accuracy: that of Apple's dictation recognizer. Good on clear speech, weaker on heavy accents, jargon and names, less accurate than large Whisper models. Both audio tracks are kept, so a call can be re-transcribed later with another tool.
- Robustness: each recognized sentence is saved immediately; both audio tracks are written to disk during the call; a dropped microphone is reconnected within seconds. No length limit.
- Recording consent: Scribe does not announce itself. Users are responsible for following local recording laws.

## Good fit

- You're often on other people's meetings, where your notetaker bot can't get in or would be awkward.
- You want a transcript to paste into your own AI, not another notes app or workspace.
- You want something free, local and light that doesn't need an account.
- A backup next to Fathom, Granola, Otter or similar, for calls where the bot fails.

## Not a fit

- You want AI-written summaries, action items and a searchable meeting archive built in: use Granola or Fathom.
- You need the most accurate possible transcript, or to transcribe existing recordings: use MacWhisper.
- You need each participant on a group call identified by name: use a bot-based notetaker.
- You're on Windows, Linux, iPhone or an older macOS.

## Compared

| | Scribe | Fathom | Granola | MacWhisper |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How it hears the call | On your Mac | A bot joins | On your Mac | On your Mac |
| Works on others' meetings without asking | Yes | Only if the bot is admitted | Yes | Yes |
| Engine | Built into macOS | Cloud | Cloud | Whisper models you download |
| Account | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Price | Free, open source | Free tier, paid plans | Free tier, paid from $14/month | Free version, paid Pro |
